place-work.text: Carved galleries, water disposal and religious upkeep linked different kinds of work. Source-specific form, interpretation and conservation evidence explain a built religious landscape without reconstructing one labor system, secure founder or universal itinerary.

evidence.text: A conserved monumental site combines early fabric with later intervention.

production.text: Terraces, carved reliefs and stupas required coordinated building and carving.

name: Borobudur: a landscape for Buddhist ideas
geographicPrecision: Temple-site locator; no inference of a regional political boundary.

interval.label: Built in the eighth–ninth centuries CE
interval.note: Broad construction frame from UNESCO, not exact building dates or the entire duration of use.

question: How can movement through a building teach an idea?
summary: Borobudur joins a built hill, carved stories and spaces for movement. Builders and carvers organized stone surfaces while upkeep linked religious institutions to resources and people. Evidence for those relationships comes from the monument, modern studies, attributed inscription interpretation and later conservation; each answers a different question.

sections.title: A building organized around a hill
sections.text: UNESCO describes five concentric square terraces below three circular platforms and a crowning stupa, built around a natural hill. Walls and balustrades carry reliefs; seventy-two openwork stupas surround the central upper stupa and change the surrounding forms. Stonework and carving therefore made both spaces to enter and surfaces to attend to. UNESCO relates the arrangement to Buddhist cosmology. A modern schematic helps distinguish its shapes, but supplies neither a measured survey nor a record of any visitor’s thoughts.

sections.title: Stories included recognizable kinds of buildings
sections.text: Hari Setyawan’s study examines wooden-building roofs represented in the reliefs. It compares forms and story settings to interpret dwellings, storage buildings, halls and monastic spaces. Those settings make practical activities part of a religious narrative world: sheltering, gathering and storing matter alongside carved figures. The study locates Lalitavistara on the upper first-gallery wall and Gandavyuha on later gallery walls. Reading a sequence means attending to a scene’s position as well as its carved content. Comparing those locations makes the relationship between a story and an architectural surface inspectable. These are interpretations of depicted architecture, not recovered floor plans or a census of the households living beside the monument.

sections.title: Moving water required continued work
sections.text: Rain falling on terraces had to leave the structure. The conservation encyclopedia describes earlier drainage through jaladwara, or water spouts, toward lower levels and the hill. It distinguishes this from pipes, infiltration wells and inspection basins introduced during the second restoration. Water disposal connects the monument’s form with recurrent inspection and repair. The 2008 photograph consequently shows a surviving conserved building; it cannot separate all early stones from twentieth-century interventions by appearance alone.

sections.title: Support reached beyond the carved stone
sections.text: Religious upkeep also needed resources. BorobudurPedia interprets the 842 Tri Tepusan inscription as land privileges supporting a religious foundation connected with Borobudur. That account offers a concrete way to ask how surrounding production could contribute to maintenance, without recovering every payment or naming a certain founder. In the present landscape, a December 2025 exhibition documented builders, carpenters, potters and other practitioners sharing local architectural knowledge. Their work gives neighboring communities a visible role today, without making their houses unchanged survivals from the construction centuries.

claims.text: The monumental construction dates broadly to the eighth–ninth centuries, and its present form includes modern restoration.

placeStudy.title: Borobudur, Pawon and Mendut: three component references
placeStudy.description: Published modern World Heritage component coordinates orient three distinct monuments. They are not exact entrances or archaeological findpoints. UNESCO describes the associated temples on an alignment; no connecting itinerary, path, political boundary or shared construction episode is reconstructed here. No coastline or unsourced ancient settlement is drawn.

deeperReading.title: A reading convention is evidence with a purpose
deeperReading.text: Setyawan describes an east-start clockwise convention for reading and numbering reliefs, retaining an earlier sequence while adding quadrant codes. That convention helps locate passages for comparison; Table 1 associates galleries and walls or balustrades with narrative cycles. It does not turn the unlabelled schematic into a measured panel plan or show that every ancient visitor followed a single mandatory itinerary. A numbered research sequence and an individual’s religious experience are different questions.

citations.locator: Printed pp. 141–143 / PDF 5–7: method and Table 1

deeperReading.title: Patronage needs the right document and translation
deeperReading.text: The 842 interpretation above comes from a modern institutional encyclopedia. The separately consulted Kayumwungan digital edition supplies English only for stanzas 12 and 14, not its complete Old Javanese grant section. It is also a different inscription. These limited translated stanzas cannot silently become a full Tri Tepusan translation or a secure Borobudur foundation biography. UNESCO’s broad Syailendra attribution remains distinct from identifying one patron, collecting actual revenues or recovering labor conditions.

deeperReading.title: A living landscape includes disagreement
deeperReading.text: The December 2024 monitoring mission heard vendor and resident concerns about access, relocation and benefits, and recommended further engagement. Those mediated accounts complicate any picture of a monument with one unanimous surrounding community. The later architecture exhibition documents another form of participation, not proof that every concern was resolved. Likewise, a modern Cultural Axis Path project linking the monuments cannot establish an ancient procession. Source date, purpose and the people represented remain part of the explanation.

evidenceReading.title: What can a plan, a story and an upkeep account establish?
evidenceReading.introduction: The following are editorial paraphrases of distinct modern sources. Source images, architectural interpretation and limited inscription consultation must not be merged into one eyewitness account.

items.label: A schematic organizes forms, not a visitor’s experience
items.text: Indon’s 2007 schematic shows square and circular forms and stair-like projections. It has no north arrow or scale. Setyawan separately records an east-start clockwise relief-reading convention.
items.interpretation: The diagram supports visible form comparisons; the study supplies a documented research/reading convention. Neither recovers one required ancient itinerary, exact panel coordinates or every visitor’s thoughts. No inspected measured survey lies behind this adoption.

citations.locator: Inspected source pixels and file metadata

items.label: Depicted roofs require comparison and interpretation
items.text: Setyawan compares roof forms and story settings to interpret several kinds of wooden buildings, including dwellings and storage or gathering places. The study explicitly limits what a partial depiction can recover.
items.interpretation: Architectural distinctions make practical settings legible in narratives. A scene is not a measured household plan, a population count or direct proof of the homes beside Borobudur. The study’s inconsistent six/seven roof-type totals are not resolved by the reader or adopted as a count.

citations.locator: Printed pp. 140–143 and 161–162; abstract versus conclusion

items.label: An upkeep interpretation is not a complete foundation record
items.text: BorobudurPedia connects Tri Tepusan 842 and Sri Kahulunan with land privileges for religious upkeep. The different Kayumwungan edition has only two consulted English stanzas, outside a complete translated grant section.
items.interpretation: The institutional interpretation supports a question about resources sustaining religion. It does not establish a certain founder, fulfilled payments or a complete local labor system. The partial English edition cannot fill those gaps by being treated as the same document.

familyActivity.title: Forms, movement and evidence still needed
steps: Look at the supplied modern schematic. Find one square form and one circular form; describe how they differ without using a compass direction.
Read the source capsule with an adult if useful. Make two cards: a visible form in the diagram, and the reading convention described by the study.
Write a claim the diagram supports about the building’s shapes. Then write one thing it cannot establish about an ancient visitor’s route or thoughts.
Compare the conserved-site photograph. Name one visible feature and one question about earlier construction or later repairs that would need another source.
familyActivity.explanation: Source capsule — editorial paraphrase: UNESCO describes square terraces below circular platforms. Setyawan’s relief study records an east-start clockwise reading/numbering convention. Indon’s 2007 schematic has no north arrow or scale and is not an inspected measured archaeological plan. Kartapranata’s 2008 photograph shows the conserved monument after major modern work. The diagram and photograph support form observations; they do not require an invented ancient visitor or prove one compulsory route.

review.reviewer: Codex selected source consultation and internal author QA; not independent historian approval
review.scope: Layered account of built form, relief interpretation, drainage, attributed patronage evidence and neighboring communities. Three evidence readings, a supplied-source family activity, separate source-qualified context and three component reference points. Full existing case identity, 700–900 interval including note/precision, claims and earlier dimensions retained. The modern source photograph and schematic retain separate creation dates, rights and interpretive limits; no measured archaeological plan or required ancient itinerary is reconstructed.
limitations: UNESCO’s broad construction, Santiko’s study-specific cultural frame, attributed 842 interpretation, uncertain tenth–fifteenth-century end-of-use wording and modern restoration remain different dates. The 700–1000 reference does not extend the unchanged 700–900 case or assert one polity.

Setyawan consultation covers selected web-PDF text, not all 28 pages or figure pixels. Roof-only/partial depictions do not recover household dimensions, a census, exact material structures or a full village. Inconsistent six/seven roof-type totals remain unresolved; no type count adopted.
Only the Santiko abstract was read; underlying Buddhist texts and full article were not consulted. Its cultural frame is attributed rather than a new date for every relief or the complete building.

Tri Tepusan patronage/upkeep is a modern institutional interpretation, not a complete freshly read primary translation. Kayumwungan is a different record with only stanzas 12/14 available in the consulted English translation. No secure individual founder, exact labor system, actual revenue or compliance inferred.

Three UNESCO component coordinates are geographic references, not entrances, excavated points, a measured monument plan, household locations, ancient boundary or movement route. The modern Cultural Axis Path project cannot supply a guessed ancient itinerary.

Indon’s 2007 diagram is a source schematic with no north/scale/legend; no underlying measured survey was inspected. Source geometry is not traced into an original guide. The separate 2009 diagram with a flagged niche-count error is rejected as a verified inventory. No close-up relief image or complete measured archaeological plan adopted.

The two source images were actually inspected and hashed; source pixels are retained in research captures. Their CC BY-SA 3.0 photograph/diagram rights remain distinct from building public-domain status and any future original artwork. The 2008 photograph’s exact day and compass direction remain conflicting; no unsupported resolution supplied.

The 2024 mission report was consulted only in selected web-PDF sections, not all 81 pages or image pixels. Community voices are mediated and incomplete; recommendations are not completed implementation. The 2025 exhibition and 2026 article do not establish unbroken ancient-household continuity.

Source consultation and internal author checks do not establish independent historian/community approval, real family usability, human screen-reader or physical-device behavior, or physical print quality. Those acceptance tasks remain open; automated validation is recorded separately in the dated candidate receipt.
